phases.name: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
phases.description: Freeze the supplied advertising brief, create the advertiser control plane, and establish consent-aware audience inputs before selecting ads.

phases.name: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
phases.description: Filter for lawful eligibility first, then combine campaign pacing, frequency caps, experiments, and bounded real-time bidding on the feed path.

phases.name: Deliver, verify events, and reconcile spend
phases.description: Connect ad delivery to an at-least-once measurement pipeline, apply fraud controls, reconcile immutable billing entries, and scale from measured peaks.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Read the exact brief and mark decisions it leaves open
steps.content: The frozen problem is Develop an Ads Management and Display System for a Social Feed: Design an advertising platform for targeting, serving, and billing ads in social media feeds. Requirements: Create and manage ad campaigns; Target ads by demographics and interests; Serve ads in user feeds; Track impressions and clicks; Billing and budget management; A/B testing for ad creatives; Fraud detection and prevention; Handle billions of ad impressions per day; Real-time bidding support. Constraints: Low latency for ad serving (<100ms); Fair ad distribution; Accurate tracking and attribution; Privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA); Prevent click fraud. The hints are Ad ranking and auction algorithms; User profiling for targeting; Real-time bidding infrastructure; Impression/click tracking pipeline; Machine learning for optimization. Hints are prompts, not additional requirements. The brief does not specify consent semantics, sensitive-category rules, a fairness metric, auction/pricing rules, billing events, attribution windows, retention, currency handling, the latency percentile, or peak traffic. This review draft makes provisional choices below and marks policy owners' decisions for review; none is a claim of legal approval or production capacity.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add the advertiser campaign console
steps.content: Advertisers create, edit, pause, and inspect campaigns through an authenticated console. Validate creative assets, dates, audience rules, budget, bid, currency, and the selected buying model before a campaign can become eligible. Keep draft edits distinct from the active version used by auctions.

component.label: Advertiser Console
component.description: Campaign setup, creative experiments, and spend reporting

properties.purpose: Let authenticated advertisers create and manage versioned campaigns, upload creatives, configure targeting, budget, bid, buying model and A/B variants, then review delivery and reconciled spend.

component.highlightReason: This existing Web App catalog component represents the advertiser-facing campaign workflow.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add the ads API gateway
steps.content: Use one catalog gateway for advertiser operations, feed ad-decision requests, and signed measurement events, with separate routes, authorization scopes, validation, and rate limits. Keep event ingestion asynchronous after a bounded acceptance response; it must not wait for billing or analytics.

component.label: Ads API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated campaign, decision, and event routes

properties.purpose: Validate and route separately authorized advertiser, feed-decision, and signed impression/click requests; enforce request bounds and protect the latency-sensitive decision path.

component.highlightReason: The API Gateway catalog type covers the existing platform's authenticated HTTP entry point.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add campaign lifecycle and validation
steps.content: The service owns campaign state transitions and publishes an immutable active configuration version only after validation. Preserve targeting, bid, budget, creative, experiment, and buying-model versions with each decision so later reports and billing can explain which rules were applied.

component.label: Campaign Service
component.description: Campaign validation, versioning, and advertiser reporting

properties.purpose: Validate campaign schedules, targeting, budgets, bids, buying models, creatives and experiment variants; publish versioned active state and expose advertiser reporting without putting writes on feed reads.

component.highlightReason: The Backend Server catalog type represents the campaign domain service without adding a new component type.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Persist campaign versions and budget policy
steps.content: Store campaign status, schedule, targeting rules, bid and budget limits, currency, buying model, creative versions, and experiment configuration. Treat this durable store as the source for campaign state, while the decision path consumes bounded, versioned snapshots rather than scanning it per feed request.

component.label: Campaign Configuration Store
component.description: Durable source of campaign and experiment versions

properties.purpose: Persist versioned campaign status, schedules, targeting, bids, currency, budgets, buying models, creative references and experiment definitions as the durable control-plane source.

component.highlightReason: The Database catalog type stores durable campaign configuration and reporting state.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Keep creative assets separate from campaign metadata
steps.content: Store validated creative files under immutable or versioned references; keep moderation state, dimensions, destination URL, and campaign ownership in campaign metadata. A creative cannot enter an experiment or auction until validation and review have completed.

component.label: Creative Asset Store
component.description: Versioned image, video, and approved creative assets

properties.purpose: Store validated, versioned ad creative assets separately from campaign metadata and expose only approved assets through controlled delivery references.

component.highlightReason: The existing Object Storage catalog component fits large creative files without inventing a storage type.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Choose a versioned campaign contract
steps.content: The brief asks for campaign creation and management but does not define activation or edit semantics. This draft publishes immutable active versions and records the version on each auction, event, and ledger entry.

decision.question: How should an edit to a live campaign affect decisions already in flight?
decision.chosen: Activate a new validated version atomically and retain the old version for in-flight decision and event attribution
decision.chosenReason: A decision, impression, or invoice can then be reproduced against the exact targeting, creative, budget, and buying rules it observed.

alternatives.option: Mutate active campaign rows in place
alternatives.tradeoff: An event arriving later may no longer identify the rules or creative actually served.

alternatives.option: Require every edit to create a separate campaign
alternatives.tradeoff: It burdens operators and fragments reporting for ordinary revisions.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Make targeting an eligibility rule, not a data license
steps.content: Demographics and interests are campaign inputs only when their collection and use are consented, disclosed, purpose-limited, and legally permitted for the user's region. The working assumption is to exclude sensitive categories and inferred sensitive traits. A contextual-only path remains available when personalization is unavailable; legal basis, age rules, consent wording, retention, and regional policy still need owner review.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add the social feed client
steps.content: The client requests an ad slot as part of a feed page and renders only the returned approved creative reference. It sends signed impression and click events with event IDs; a client callback is evidence to validate, not proof that an impression or click is billable.

component.label: Social Feed Client
component.description: Feed slot request, ad rendering, and signed event callbacks

properties.purpose: Request an ad slot with permitted feed context, render an approved creative reference, and submit signed impression/click event IDs for server-side validation.

component.highlightReason: The Web App catalog type represents the existing social feed surface where ads are displayed.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add the feed integration
steps.content: The feed service requests a bounded ad decision after assembling the placement context. It returns the feed without holding the whole page open for an unavailable bidder; the platform's <100ms constraint applies to ad serving, and the official timing boundary and percentile must be confirmed.

component.label: Feed Ad Integration
component.description: Placement context and bounded ad decision integration

properties.purpose: Call the ad decision path with placement context, enforce its deadline, and return an approved creative or no-fill without blocking the social feed on a slow external bidder.

component.highlightReason: The Backend Server catalog component models the feed's server-side placement integration.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Add a consent and policy gate
steps.content: Resolve the user's current region and consent/opt-out state before any personalized profile lookup. The gate returns an explicit allowed mode and policy version; missing, stale, or contradictory consent state fails to contextual-only selection rather than silently enabling profiling.

component.label: Consent and Ads Policy Gate
component.description: Region, consent, opt-out, and deletion policy decisions

properties.purpose: Resolve region and current consent or opt-out policy before personalized targeting; return a versioned allowed mode and fail to contextual-only when policy state is unavailable.

component.highlightReason: The Auth Service catalog type supplies an existing security boundary for the consent decision.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Keep consent state and deletion work auditable
steps.content: Persist purpose, region, consent version, opt-out, and data deletion state with restricted access and an auditable change trail. Propagate withdrawal and deletion to profile indexes and caches; keep only the minimum event and financial records allowed by the reviewed retention policy.

component.label: Consent and Privacy Store
component.description: Versioned user ad-consent and suppression state

properties.purpose: Persist versioned ad consent, region, opt-out, suppression and deletion state with restricted access and an audit trail; drive removal from derived audience indexes.

component.highlightReason: The Database catalog type supports durable and reviewable privacy-policy state.

steps.phase: Define the campaign contract and policy inputs
steps.title: Index only permitted audience signals
steps.content: Build queryable demographic and interest segments from approved, purpose-limited signals. Keep provenance and policy version with a segment, exclude sensitive categories, and support deletion/opt-out propagation. Do not put raw identifiers or unreviewed profile features into the online candidate index.

component.label: Permitted Audience Index
component.description: Consent-gated audience segment lookup

properties.purpose: Find campaign candidates from approved demographic and interest segments while retaining policy provenance, excluding sensitive traits, and propagating deletion and opt-out changes.

component.highlightReason: The existing Search catalog type provides an index for fast segment candidate lookup.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Choose the no-consent behavior
steps.content: GDPR and CCPA are named constraints, not complete implementation specifications. This draft treats missing consent, a withdrawal, or a CCPA opt-out as a hard stop for cross-session personalized targeting and uses contextual-only campaigns; the user remains eligible for the feed itself.

decision.question: What may the decision path use when personalized ads are not allowed?
decision.chosen: Use contextual placement and non-sensitive campaign rules; do not query or persist a cross-session profile for ad selection
decision.chosenReason: The fallback keeps serving possible while honoring the consent gate and avoiding a hidden profiling fallback.

alternatives.option: Use the profile but suppress only reporting
alternatives.tradeoff: Targeting itself still uses data after the user has opted out or withdrawn consent.

alternatives.option: Suppress every ad and the feed
alternatives.tradeoff: It couples an advertising choice to access to the underlying social feed.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Add the eligibility-first ad decision service
steps.content: Apply hard checks for campaign status, schedule, placement, policy, audience, creative approval, budget reservation, and frequency cap before ranking. Only then compare eligible internal candidates with bounded exchange bids. Record the chosen campaign, auction, creative and policy versions for later event attribution.

component.label: Ad Decision and Auction Service
component.description: Eligibility, constrained ranking, and bounded auction

properties.purpose: Filter campaign, placement, consent, creative, pacing and frequency eligibility before ranking; run a bounded internal/external auction and record versioned decision context for attribution.

component.highlightReason: The Backend Server catalog type represents the low-latency decision and auction logic.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Reserve budget and enforce frequency caps atomically
steps.content: Use a fast distributed store for atomic campaign budget reservations and consent-eligible frequency counters. Reservations prevent concurrent regions from overserving the same remaining budget; reconcile them against accepted billable events and release expired or rejected reservations idempotently. It is a serving guard, not the financial source of truth.

component.label: Pacing and Frequency State
component.description: Atomic serving reservations and bounded frequency counters

properties.purpose: Make atomic campaign-budget reservations and enforce campaign/user frequency caps using consent-eligible pseudonymous keys; reconcile reservations to the financial ledger.

component.highlightReason: The Cache catalog type represents low-latency counters; the durable ledger remains authoritative for charges.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Add the real-time bidding adapter
steps.content: The adapter sends only the permitted request fields to configured demand partners, signs and validates bid responses, and rejects late, malformed, wrong-currency, or ineligible bids. The brief does not name an exchange protocol or partner contract; treat those as integration decisions and keep partner calls isolated behind this adapter.

component.label: RTB Exchange Adapter
component.description: Bounded external bid requests and response validation

properties.purpose: Call configured real-time bidding partners with policy-approved fields, enforce deadlines, validate signed bid responses and currency, and isolate partner failures from feed delivery.

component.highlightReason: The API Gateway catalog type supports the existing bounded HTTP integration pattern for external bidding.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Turn the <100ms constraint into a measurable deadline
steps.content: The brief supplies an ad-serving ceiling of <100ms, so the operational goal is to return an ad payload or no-fill in under 100 ms; it gives no percentile or measurement endpoints. Working review assumption: measure from the feed slot request reaching the feed integration until the result is ready; reserve at most 70ms for the decision service and 30ms for feed integration/transport. Inside the service, fetch consent and candidate snapshots in parallel, give external bids a bounded deadline (30ms is an initial design assumption), then leave time for eligibility, ranking, and response. Confirm the percentile and stage budgets with the product owner and representative load tests; do not describe these draft budgets as measured SLOs.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Bound exchange waits and choose a safe fallback
steps.content: Run internal candidate retrieval and permitted exchange calls concurrently under the remaining deadline. If an exchange misses its cutoff, ignore that response; do not extend the feed request to rescue an external bid.

decision.question: What should happen when the real-time bidding deadline expires?
decision.chosen: Rank already eligible internal campaigns if available; otherwise return no-fill and continue the feed
decision.chosenReason: A bounded fallback protects the <100ms ad-serving constraint and avoids billing for an ad that was not selected and rendered.

alternatives.tradeoff: A slow partner can consume the full feed latency budget or stall the page.

alternatives.option: Accept the first unvalidated late response
alternatives.tradeoff: It bypasses eligibility, currency, auction ordering, and reproducible decision records.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Separate campaign pacing from user frequency
steps.content: Pacing limits campaign spend and delivery over the campaign's configured period; smooth reservations toward that campaign's own budget and schedule, then correct against ledgered billable events. Frequency caps limit repeated exposure for a campaign or advertiser over a configured window. Use a first-party pseudonymous key only when policy permits; otherwise use a session-level cap or no persistent cap. A fairness rule should prevent eligible campaigns from starving solely due to volume, while respecting bids, relevance, budgets, and contracts; the owner must define the fairness metric and tie-break policy.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Deliver approved creative assets from the edge
steps.content: Return an opaque approved asset reference from the decision path and serve the versioned creative through the CDN. Do not cache personalized decision responses as public content; support rapid invalidation for withdrawn or disapproved creatives.

component.label: Creative Delivery CDN
component.description: Versioned approved creative delivery

properties.purpose: Serve versioned approved creative assets from the edge while keeping personalized ad-decision responses private and supporting invalidation of withdrawn or disapproved assets.

component.highlightReason: The CDN catalog component serves static creative assets without caching user-specific auction decisions.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Accept signed impression and click events
steps.content: Validate event signature, schema, campaign/creative/auction reference, event ID, and replay window, then acknowledge durable queue acceptance. Keep event-time and ingest-time distinct. Never count a client callback twice because a browser or network retried it.

component.label: Measurement Event Ingest
component.description: Validated, deduplicable impression and click intake

properties.purpose: Validate signed impression/click event envelopes, decision references, event IDs and replay bounds, then durably enqueue accepted events without synchronous analytics or billing work.

component.highlightReason: The existing API Gateway catalog type represents bounded event acceptance at the public edge.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Buffer the high-volume event stream
steps.content: Partition accepted events for parallel consumption and replay, retaining event IDs and campaign/auction references. Delivery is at least once: consumers must be idempotent, offsets and lag observable, and retention long enough for the reviewed replay and reconciliation needs.

component.label: Impression and Click Event Broker
component.description: Durable partitioned event transport for measurement and billing

properties.purpose: Buffer and partition accepted ad events for independent fraud, attribution, analytics, and billing consumers; preserve replayability and assume at-least-once delivery.

component.highlightReason: The Message Broker catalog type supports scalable, replayable fan-out to downstream event consumers.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Detect invalid and suspicious click activity
steps.content: Deduplicate by event ID and decision reference; check signatures, replay, impossible rates, repeated patterns, and configured bot/fraud signals. Keep expensive cross-event analysis asynchronous so click fraud defenses do not add unbounded work to ad selection. Quarantine uncertain events for review instead of silently deleting accounting evidence.

component.label: Fraud and Attribution Processor
component.description: Idempotent event validation, click-fraud signals, and attribution

properties.purpose: Deduplicate and validate ad events, detect click-fraud patterns, apply versioned attribution rules, and quarantine uncertain events without delaying the feed decision path.

component.highlightReason: The Stream Processor catalog type supports high-volume, stateful event validation and attribution.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Record billable events in an immutable ledger
steps.content: Persist idempotent charge entries with campaign, auction, creative/variant, event ID, buying-model version, accepted billable event, price snapshot, currency, and policy references. Keep reservations and estimates separate from posted charges; late fraud findings create explicit reversal or credit entries rather than rewriting history.

component.label: Advertiser Billing Ledger
component.description: Immutable, idempotent campaign charge and adjustment records

properties.purpose: Append idempotent billable-event charges and explicit reversals with campaign, auction, creative variant, model version, price, currency and event provenance.

component.highlightReason: The Database catalog type is the durable financial record, separate from fast pacing counters.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Reconcile delivery, charges, budgets, and invoices
steps.content: Compare accepted decisions and deduplicated validated billable events with ledger entries and campaign budget reservations by campaign, period, buying model, and currency. Explain unmatched, duplicate, late, reversed, or quarantined events; issue auditable adjustments and invoice totals from ledger records, not raw client counters.

component.label: Billing Reconciliation Service
component.description: Event-to-ledger reconciliation and advertiser invoice preparation

properties.purpose: Reconcile accepted billable events, auction records, pacing reservations and immutable ledger entries by campaign, period and currency; explain variances and produce auditable invoice totals.

component.highlightReason: The Backend Server catalog type supports explicit reconciliation and invoice preparation logic.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Store aggregate delivery and experiment outcomes
steps.content: Build advertiser reports, attribution summaries, A/B results, pacing diagnostics, and capacity trends from validated events. Use consent-aware retention and aggregation; keep raw identifiers out of general analytics and preserve experiment assignment and campaign-version labels for comparable results.

component.label: Ads Analytics Warehouse
component.description: Aggregated campaign, attribution, experiment, and capacity data

properties.purpose: Store policy-aware aggregates for campaign reporting, attribution, A/B comparisons, fraud diagnostics and capacity planning without exposing raw identifiers broadly.

component.highlightReason: The Data Warehouse catalog type supports analytical workloads separately from feed serving and financial writes.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Observe serving, privacy, events, and finance separately
steps.content: Measure decision latency by stage and percentile, no-fill and timeout rates, campaign under-delivery, budget reservation drift, frequency-cap hits, consent-mode decisions, event lag/deduplication, suspected fraud, ledger variance, and deletion propagation. Keep dashboards and traces free of raw profiles or unnecessary personal data.

component.label: Ads Platform Monitoring
component.description: Latency, fairness, privacy, event, fraud, and billing health

properties.purpose: Track decision stage latency, timeouts, campaign delivery fairness, reservation drift, consent outcomes, event lag, fraud signals, ledger variances and privacy deletion propagation with minimized telemetry.

component.highlightReason: The Monitoring catalog type covers operational signals without adding a custom component.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Scale from peak rate and skew evidence
steps.content: One billion impressions per day averages about 11.6k per second; the brief says billions per day, but supplies no peak-to-average ratio, regional split, event bytes, or campaign skew. Use partitioned event processing and campaign/region-aware serving keys, then size partitions and consumers from measured bursts, hot campaigns, queue age, and decision latency rather than choosing an unsupported fixed fleet size.

scaleTrigger.metric: Observed peak impressions and clicks per second, partition skew, queue age, decision latency, and reservation contention
scaleTrigger.action: Add capacity or repartition only after identifying hot campaign and regional keys; preserve idempotent replay and atomic budget reservations
scaleTrigger.impact: Builds a testable path toward billions of ad impressions per day while avoiding an average-rate-only capacity claim.

steps.phase: Gate candidates and decide inside the latency budget
steps.title: Make creative experiments reproducible
steps.content: Choose a campaign-scoped assignment using a stable pseudonymous key only when policy allows; otherwise assign at session scope. Persist experiment and variant IDs on the decision and validated events, keep control/treatment eligibility equivalent, and avoid moving a person between variants during a configured experiment.

decision.question: How should the platform assign and measure A/B creative variants?
decision.chosen: Use deterministic campaign-scoped assignment with consent-aware identity, explicit control/treatment versions, and event-level experiment IDs
decision.chosenReason: Stable assignment reduces cross-arm contamination and lets validated impressions, clicks, and billing be tied to the creative actually selected.

alternatives.option: Choose a random creative on every request
alternatives.tradeoff: Repeated exposure can cross arms and makes user-level comparisons noisy.

alternatives.option: Use a stable account identifier for every user
alternatives.tradeoff: It ignores opt-out and regional limits on persistent profiling.

steps.title: Review the unresolved policy and capacity gates
steps.content: Before treating this local draft as a reviewed design, confirm the consent/legal basis and retention rules, sensitive-category exclusions, fairness definition, first-price versus second-price and CPM/CPC contracts, attribution windows, event acceptance and reversal policy, official <100ms percentile/boundary, exchange deadlines, currency/rounding rules, and peak traffic profile. Verify deletion propagation, duplicate replay, late fraud reversals, budget races across regions, and invoice reconciliation with representative fixtures and load. The graph is a review draft; it does not claim those product decisions or operational results are settled.
